references.text: Pharaoh asks, 'Who is the Lord?' - here God shows that He is the Lord through signs and wonders
God declares that the Egyptians will know that He is the Lord when He stretches out His hand
The fulfillment of the prophecy that water will turn to blood
God warns Moses about the sign of water from the Nile turning to blood
The psalmist reminds us that God turned the rivers into blood in Egypt
The psalmist recalls that God turned the water into blood
Ezekiel uses the same expression: they will know that I am the Lord
In Revelation, the waters turn to blood, reflecting the plagues of Egypt
The two witnesses have power to turn water into blood, as Moses did
Repetition of the central prophetic theme: God's intervention (miracle or judgment) aims for the people to 'know' that He is the Lord.
Repetition of the theological purpose: God's judgment on an enemy (the Nile/Sidon) serves to reveal that He is the Lord.
Common theological structure: Judgment (regardless of form) leads to the recognition of the Lord's identity.
